result.region: Frostpeak Highlands: new Glass Lake (镜湖) east of the existing Frostpeak massif cluster; lake south end
result.summary:
I've planned 1128 as the south end of a new long alpine lake, the Glass Lake, east of the existing Frostpeak cluster. The lake runs north-south from z -700 to -4450, between x 1700 and x 3050. The cluster (east_spur, east_summit, frost_crown, west_summit) forms the lake's west wall and is the left group of peaks. A new east wall of massif prefab instances forms the right group, and a new north range (shared with 1276) supplies the smaller, more distant peaks in the centre.

How I checked it: I read every terrain GLB and massif GLB in the world and built a height grid plus a crude flat-shaded software renderer with mirror reflections, all in scratchpad/lake1128/. Rendered from this camera with the proposed geometry, the frame matches the reference composition closely: a ring of snow peaks across the full width, mirror water over the lower half, a pine islet at left, a distant islet in the centre and a rock at lower right. Side-by-side renders against all four references are in scratchpad/lake1128/ref_vs_plan.png, and the geometry spec is in plan_geo.py.

Projection check (1672x941 pixels, x then y):
- west_summit (100,250) and frost_crown (320,230): the left big peaks. The reference has them at about (90,280).
- east_summit (410,305).
- North range N1, N3 and N2 at about (680 to 965, 265 to 295).
- East wall E1 (1255,277) and E2 (1420,246): the right big peaks. The reference has them at about (1370,290).
- E3 spur (1690,284).
- Left islet (308,542), far islet (801,464), rock (1375,737).
- Horizon is at about y 445, set by a 1.45 degree downward pitch.

Our peaks sit about 40 px higher in frame than the reference; this is acceptable for a 60-point pass.

Lighting: soft late-morning light from the west-southwest, behind the camera on its left. This matches the lit left faces of the mountains in the reference.

Camera height: y_abs is authoritative. The camera is 22 m above the future water level, and the current ground at this spot is 21.7 m. Once the lake exists this reads as 22 m above the water.

Effect on the opening view (1343): the north range appears as a second row of peaks behind the Frostpeak cluster in the opening camera. No new foreground blocks anything, and the range gets bigger, which is closer to the 1343 reference. The 1343 owner should still check it.

Scratchpad note: the scratchpad root is shared with sibling agents. I briefly renamed a sibling's glb.py and then restored it with identical content and the same timestamp. All my own files are now in lake1128/.

result.region: Frostpeak Highlands: north gorge (高山雪峡) above the Glass Lake's north end
result.summary:
1276 is the mouth of a new gorge north of the Glass Lake. The gorge is formed by the scaled massif instances in the north range, shared with 1128, 1129 and 1344. The camera floats at y 300 above the lake's north end and looks north up the gorge, tilted 1.5 degrees upward.

In the crude render:
- The left wall (N1, west_summit at scale 1.8) rises out of the frame at the top left; its peak projects to (163,-49).
- The right wall (N2, frost_crown at scale 1.7) has a sharp lit face at the right, with its peak at (1652,-1) in the top-right corner.
- The end peak (N3, needle_ridge at scale 3.0) is centred at (890,207), close to the reference's centre peak at about (850,150 to 200).
- The right-centre peak (N5) is at (1254,294), against about (1300,280) in the reference.
- N4 sits at (469,360).

The two near walls meet in a V at about y 170 near z -5100, so the camera stays south of the walls. Without the cloud floor, the green terrain at y 20 shows at the bottom of the gorge.

Main gaps: the cloud floor at about y 200, the blizzard, and the big flat facets that come from scaling the massifs 1.7 to 3.0 times. The reference walls are finely faceted with patches of snow and dark rock.

Lighting: bright sun from the west, slightly north. The left wall's faces toward the camera stay in blue shadow, while the right wall's inner faces and the centre peak's west face are lit, as in the reference.

On scale: I kept all scales uniform, because non-uniform scaling of collision shapes is unreliable in Godot.

Camera height: y_abs 300 is authoritative. Today's ground here is 19.3 m, which will become water after the lake cut.

This gorge also works as the setting for 1275 (the cliff port in a blizzard) if that plan wants it.

The river leaves the lake's south-east shore at (2900,-1150), winds south past two ponds to (2780,380), then turns west along low ground (20 to 40 m) toward Amberfield at (1500,900). I rerouted it after finding my first route climbed the dome's lower slope at 130 m.
